title: To expand the sharing of information with respect to suspected violations of intellectual property rights in trade.
official_title: To expand the sharing of information with respect to suspected violations of intellectual property rights in trade.
summary: When customs agents suspect imported goods are counterfeit or pirated, they can already ask brand owners to help identify violations — but only certain information can be shared. This bill expands that program to let CBP share nonpublic data generated by online marketplaces, freight forwarders, and express consignment operators with brand owners and any other party the Commissioner determines has an interest in the merchandise. It also broadens the physical evidence that can be shared to include packing materials and containers, and requires CBP to notify the recipient of any nonpublic information it transmits.
brief: Expands what counterfeit-goods intelligence CBP can share with brand owners — adding marketplace and freight data, packing materials, and a broader circle of eligible recipients.

top_lines.headline: Counterfeit Goods Detection
subs: CBP can now share nonpublic data from online marketplaces, freight forwarders, and express consignment operators with brand owners
Packing materials and containers added to physical evidence that can be shared
CBP must notify the recipient of nonpublic information it transmits

top_lines.headline: Broader Access
subs: Adds "any other party with an interest in the merchandise" as an eligible recipient, at the Commissioner's discretion
Standard for sharing changed from "suspects" to "has a reasonable suspicion"

likelihoodReason: The bill has bipartisan sponsorship (Moore R-UT and Schneider D-IL) and 6 cosponsors, and anti-counterfeiting measures attract broad support. However, the Senate calendar for narrowly focused trade bills is unpredictable, and the expansion of data-sharing to cover marketplace and freight operator nonpublic information may draw scrutiny over privacy and due process for importers.

sections.label: Section 1 — Expansion of CBP Information Sharing

items.main: Amends Section 628A(a) of the Tariff Act of 1930 (19 U.S.C. 1628a) to authorize CBP to share nonpublic information generated by online marketplaces, express consignment operators, freight forwarders, and other importation-chain entities with parties requesting assistance in identifying IP violations.
items.detail: CBP may provide a requesting party with nonpublic information about suspected infringing merchandise that was generated by an online marketplace or similar platform, express consignment operator, freight forwarder, or any other entity involved in the sale, importation, or facilitation of the merchandise into the United States, provided that information was provided to, shared with, or obtained by CBP. In the case of such a provision, CBP must notify the person of the information transmitted, in accordance with regulations the Secretary may prescribe. The scope of shareable physical evidence expands to include packing materials and containers, in addition to the merchandise and its packaging. The standard for initiating the sharing is changed from "suspects" to "has a reasonable suspicion."

items.main: Expands the class of parties eligible to receive CBP information to any party with an interest in the merchandise, as determined appropriate by the Commissioner.
items.detail: The bill adds a new paragraph (5) to Section 628A(b) — which lists the parties eligible to receive shared information — allowing the Commissioner to extend access to any other party with an interest in the merchandise. No statutory definition of "interest" or limit on the Commissioner's discretion to determine eligibility is provided.

underreported.summary: The bill extends information sharing to "any other party with an interest in the merchandise, as determined appropriate by the Commissioner." No statutory definition of "interest" is provided, and the Commissioner's authority to determine who qualifies is unconstrained by the bill.
underreported.why_unreported: The bill's stated purpose is expanding information sharing about suspected intellectual property rights violations. The open-ended recipient provision in paragraph (5) extends sharing to any party the Commissioner deems interested — a category that could include competitors of the importer, brokers, or other commercial parties not directly harmed by the alleged violation.

gaps: The bill authorizes sharing of nonpublic information generated by online marketplaces and freight operators but does not specify what categories of nonpublic data are covered or whether any types of data are excluded from the sharing authority.
The bill does not address the rights of the importer or the source entity (e.g., the online marketplace) to receive notice that their nonpublic information has been shared with a third party.

added: Section 628A(a)(3) of the Tariff Act of 1930 — CBP authority to share nonpublic information generated by online marketplaces, express consignment operators, freight forwarders, and other importation-chain entities with parties assisting in IP violation determinations
Section 628A(a)(4) — CBP must notify the person of nonpublic information transmitted under paragraph (3), in accordance with regulations the Secretary may prescribe
Section 628A(b)(5) — Commissioner authority to share information with any other party with an interest in the merchandise
modified: Section 628A(a) of the Tariff Act of 1930 (19 U.S.C. 1628a) — sharing threshold changed from "suspects" to "has a reasonable suspicion" of an intellectual property rights violation
Section 628A(a)(1) — physical evidence shareable with requesting parties expanded to include packing materials and containers

added: New paragraph (4): CBP must notify the person of the nonpublic information transmitted, under regulations the Secretary may prescribe
modified: Inserted text expanded to ", packing materials, containers," (was ", packing materials, shipping containers,") and now also inserts ", its packaging, packing materials, containers, and labels" after "images of the merchandise"
Paragraph (3) nonpublic-information clause restructured into a single sentence; "shared with, or obtained by" wording retained but reworded
